interpretation: The process-stable repair now passes the exact no-stub ADMIT->RESERVE->SCORE->bound SLOT->recovery COMMIT->runtime-provenance CLOSE/replay lifecycle when its ADMIT replay authority is upgraded to the provenance-aware close/replay module. The original v1 candidate had a second liveness defect: after the first provenance-aware CLOSE it attempted the next ADMIT through the historical replay layer and failed on the new reporting binding. V2 fixes that authority while preserving process-epoch permit invalidation. The integrated crash tests preserve the one-attempt rule: a score lost before durable SLOT is never relaunched and contributes fail-closed score=1, whereas a durable bound SLOT can recover COMMIT without re-running the scorer.
measurement_validity_rules: Runtime replay authority is part of the versioned scientific contract. A wrapper that can write a newer CLOSE format must use a replay authority that can read that format before issuing later ADMITs.
A score result is scientific only after its bound SLOT frame is durable. Generating a stochastic result before crash is not evidence if the SLOT never became durable.
A durable bound SLOT missing only COMMIT may recover COMMIT from immutable main-journal evidence without scorer relaunch.
Fresh process epochs must invalidate old permit MACs while still permitting read-only recovery/reconciliation from durable reservations and slots.
Torn final frames must collapse to the previous valid checksummed prefix; recovery semantics are determined only from that prefix.
scope_limitations: This is single-host cooperative POSIX execution with StableSidecarJournalIO; no multi-host/distributed fencing claim is made.
The lifecycle uses deterministic scalar scorers to validate evidence/control semantics, not production LLM inference latency or stochastic quality.

The proper-byte-cut campaign proves prefix framing behavior for the generated SLOT/COMMIT/CLOSE frames and representative repaired scientific outcomes; it does not model arbitrary corruption of already-durable earlier bytes or storage that violates fsync ordering.
